evidence.note: 'Q3 on-time departures fell on the two routes diverted around the roadworks': thesis stated up front.
'On-time departures fell from 86% to 81% in Q3, and retiming the diverted routes is the Q4 test': summary of finding and action.

'The council's 90% target counts on-time departures only, so lost mileage can rise unseen': a lost-mileage point that no neighbouring or later title picks up; s-4 resumes the on-time drop as if s-3 were absent.
'12 Cross-town and 14 Cross-town fell 14 and 11 points while the network fell 5': follows from s-1/s-2.
'Away from the roadworks the other six routes held between 85% and 90% on time': builds on s-4.
'Mill Street closed in three phases from 7 July, and routes 12 and 14 ran the diversion without retiming': gives the cause.
'Planning and the depot disagree on why 12 Cross-town fell a further 4 points in October': extends the story with a dispute.
'Retiming 12 and 14 Cross-town for the diversion is the Q4 test, checked at the end of January': near-verbatim repeat of the second clause of the s-2 title.

rationale: Titles s-4 to s-7 build cleanly from cause to evidence to dispute, and the thesis is stated at the start. But the s-3 title raises lost mileage, which connects to neither s-2 nor s-4 and never returns in a title. The s-8 title also restates the s-2 title's 'retiming is the Q4 test' almost word for word, so the titles break the argument and repeat it rather than reading as one continuous summary.
